pluginRevision: kookr-toolkit-poc@0.0.1 (synthetic POC fixture: one sentinel skill + benign hook)
reviewedBy: POC-A operator re-run for 0.2.101 / grok-4.5 (issue #1339; parity with the reviewed 0.2.93 run — identical gate verdicts and evidence values)

gates.evidence: Two independent hook sources (simulated user + Kookr monitoring) both executed for every lifecycle event in the same session (5 event types each on the toolcall run); merging across ~/.grok/hooks, ~/.claude/settings.json and plugin hooks is documented and observed.
A harmless `echo` tool call fired pre_tool_use and post_tool_use with toolName=run_terminal_command and toolInput.command; the command executed (exit 0). Stable sessionId correlates the events.

A blocking permission produces a reliable structured signal: a Kookr PreToolUse hook receives toolName+toolInput and returns an explicit deny decision; the blocked command never runs (no post_tool_use). CAVEAT (unchanged in 0.2.101): the advertised dedicated PermissionDenied event did NOT fire for --deny-rule or hook-deny blocks in headless -p; Kookr must detect blocks via PreToolUse-without-PostToolUse and its own deny decisions, not by relying on a PermissionDenied event.
A synthetic Kookr toolkit plugin placed in the (isolated) ~/.grok/plugins/ user scope is discovered by `grok inspect --json` (plugin kookr-toolkit-poc listed).
From an arbitrary cwd the model (grok-4.5) invoked the injected sentinel skill and emitted its unique token SKILL_SENTINEL_5E1D.
`grok inspect --json` lists both CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md under projectInstructions (fileType agents_md, scope project) in independent single-file cwds.

In two independent runs from non-Kookr cwds the model followed the project instruction file and returned the exact sentinels CLAUDE_SENTINEL_7F3A (CLAUDE.md-only cwd) and AGENTS_SENTINEL_9B2C (AGENTS.md-only cwd).
Under a real PTY the TUI reached readiness in 0.94s (honoring --no-alt-screen), accepted byte-level input, and the initial prompt/approval flow worked.

Success: Stop.reason=end_turn + clean exit(0) => completed. NOTE (unchanged in 0.2.101): SessionEnd does NOT fire for the parent session in headless -p, so Kookr must classify from Stop.reason + process exit, not SessionEnd. New 0.2.101 observation: subagent child sessions DO emit session_end (reason=shutdown) carrying the child subagent id.

Satisfied via the correlation path: subagent_start carries a distinct subagentId (child) vs sessionId (parent) plus subagentType. CONSTRAINT (unchanged in 0.2.101): enforceable disablement is NOT reliable — --no-subagents failed to prevent a spawn in headless -p (2 subagent_start events observed with the flag). subagent_stop was again not observed before headless process exit; the child session's session_end(reason=shutdown) event, new in this run's captures, provides a partial termination signal keyed by the child id.
SIGKILL of the owned PTY process tree drained every descendant (clean_drain=true). Default config spawns no detached leader daemon, so no orphaned backend survived.

constraints: Interactive injection: --plugin-dir is agent-only (interactive root `grok` rejects it). Toolkit distribution must sync into ~/.grok/plugins/ (mirroring the existing ~/.claude/plugins/ deploy flow); launch-scoped monitoring hooks must use per-session GROK_HOME composition, never a persistent ~/.grok mutation.

Hook schema divergence: Grok payloads are camelCase (sessionId, hookEventName, toolName, toolInput, subagentId) — a Grok-specific decoder is required; Kookr's snake_case parseHookEvent() cannot be reused unchanged.
Subagent disablement is not enforceable via tested flags; supervise children via subagent_start correlation instead of assuming they are disabled.
PermissionDenied event not observed for rule/hook denials in headless -p; detect blocks via PreToolUse-without-PostToolUse and Kookr's own deny decisions.

SessionEnd does not fire for the parent session in headless -p; rely on Stop.reason + process exit for terminal classification. Child subagent sessions do emit session_end(reason=shutdown) in 0.2.101.
Only this exact build (0.2.101 / 5bc4b5dfad / linux-x86_64 / glibc 2.35) is tested; other builds/platforms (incl. macOS) remain unqualified and may run only inside the POC runner.
Qualified with selectedModel grok-4.5 (the prior grok-build model is no longer listed by the chat proxy as of 2026-07-15); KOOKR_GROK_MODEL should be set to grok-4.5.
Chat-endpoint access requires an account entitlement (console.x.ai); a plain grok.com OAuth login returns HTTP 403 at the chat proxy until enabled.
